newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on commercials, CBOT soybeans.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on commercials, CBOT soybeans.

text.p: WCE canola ended up on commercial demand and higher Chicago soybean values.
"We followed the beans and Cargill was a good buyer," a trader said.

Jan-Mar spread at $1, Japan bought 700 Mar-May at even money, traders said. January futures crush margin rose to -38.03 from -38.76 Friday on January soyoil, meal. Volume was 4,308 lots, or 86,160 tonnes, with 230 hedges.
Japan bought 2,000 tonnes cash canola, sources said.
January canola rose $2.20 to $406.90 and March closed $2 higher at $407.60. January flax rose $1.30 to $354.30 on commercial demand. Jan-Mar spread at $3.50. Volume was 195 lots.
December feed wheat ended $1 higher at $168. March fell $0.50 to $168.20 on commercial and commission trading. Alberta Wheat Pool sold March and May, traders said. Dec-Mar spread at $1. Volume 570.

February western barley fell $0.20 at $138.90 with UGG a seller, traders said. March rose $0.30 to $138.50 on commercial and commission trading. Benson Quinn sold October down $0.10 at $136.40 to PCTS, traders said. Volume was 590 lots.
Fifteen December oats contracts rose US$4 to US$125 on commercial short covering, traders said. Peas did not trade.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats).
